newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesia says won't compromise on car policy.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says won't compromise on car policy.

text.p: Indonesia said on Tuesday it does not intend to make any compromises over its controversial car policy in its bilateral talks with Japan, the European Union EU) and the United States.
"We don't see it that way," Trade and Industry Minister Tunky Ariwibowo told Reuters when asked if Indonesia is ready to make any compromises on its national car policy.
"But we are going to discuss (it). This is a good opportunity, everybody is here now," Ariwibowo said.
He said the national car policy will remain a major policy for the country. "We want to be independent in developing our industry which we consider to be strategic for our economy," he said.
The national car policy gives tax and tariff breaks to a car company controlled by President Suharto's youngest son Hutomo Mandala Putra.

Earlier on Tuesday Terence Johnsson, sales of General Motors Corp unit PT General Motors Buana Indonesia, said the car policy had hurt GM's sales and also affected future investment plans in Indonesia.
